title: Docker
tagline: Learn containers from the Linux basics underneath to building, securing and deploying images.

credit.text: Based on the Docker roadmap from roadmap.sh (personal use)

phases.title: Prerequisites
phases.description: Get comfortable with the Linux shell and general app development before working with containers.

phases.title: Introduction & internals
phases.description: Understand what containers are, why they exist and the kernel features that make them work.
items: Bare Metal vs VMs vs Containers

phases.title: Installation & basics
phases.description: Install Docker on your machine and learn the core ideas of images and containers.

phases.title: Data persistence
phases.description: Learn why container filesystems are throwaway and how volumes and bind mounts keep data around.

phases.title: Third-party images
phases.description: Run ready-made images for databases and command line tools instead of installing them locally.

phases.title: Building images
phases.description: Write Dockerfiles that build quickly through good layer caching and produce small, safe images.

phases.title: Container registries
phases.description: Push and pull images through Docker Hub and other registries, tagging them sensibly.

phases.title: Running containers
phases.description: Start single containers and multi-container setups and tune how they run.

phases.title: Container security
phases.description: Harden both the images you ship and the containers while they run.

phases.title: Docker CLI
phases.description: Manage images, containers, volumes and networks confidently from the command line.

phases.title: Developer experience
phases.description: Make day-to-day development in containers pleasant with live reload, debugging, tests and CI.

phases.title: Deploying containers
phases.description: Ship containers to production on a platform service or an orchestrator.
